What makes the tulip so amazing?

Announcing spring in brilliant color, the tulip is an amazing flower that blooms from a bulb. It's surprising that the flower and leaves are already tucked inside a tiny bulb.

Curious about the story of the tulip picture book? We look at the lessons of the tulip picture book alongside the illustrations. Come meet the key scenes of the tulip picture book's story too. Read the tulip picture book together with your child and talk about the story.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about the tulip

Tulips reproduce mainly from a bulb, and inside the bulb the shapes of the flower and leaves are already fully formed. Planted in autumn, they must go through the cold of winter to bloom in spring. They originally come from Central Asia and Turkey, and there was even a historical event in 17th-century Netherlands called "Tulip Mania," when a single bulb could cost as much as a house.

Points to observe together

Point out things like the bulb (a home holding the flower and leaves), autumn planting and spring blooming (seasons), and the many flower colors. It's fun to talk together about "Why does it bloom in spring even though we plant it in autumn?"

Parent guide — extending through observation and hands-on play

The best way is to plant a tulip bulb yourself in autumn and observe it bloom in spring (a lesson in the seasons). Try cutting a bulb in half to show the structure inside, or comparing tulips of different colors.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Are tulips grown from seeds?
A. They reproduce mainly from bulbs. The shapes of the flower and leaves are already inside the bulb.

Q. Why does it bloom in spring even though we plant it in autumn?
A. Because it's a plant that must go through a cold winter period to bloom. The cold is the signal for it to flower.

Q. How can we observe them at home?
A. Plant a bulb in autumn and observe the spring bloom, and try looking at a cut bulb and comparing several colors.
